gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CNC Kitchen measured the Bambu Lab X2D's chamber with thermocouples, finding it reached a real 65 °C in about 20 minutes on the heater alone and in roughly half that with the bed also heating, which is the only thermocouple-measured time to the full 65 °C among the candidates; the X2D is also $589 at 3D Universe today, $60 less than the QIDI Plus4's $649 at QIDI US.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QIDI Plus4 TechSpecs page, which gives no heat-up times; the cited desktop3dprinters.us chamber-temperature list, which says 'Not listed' for heat-up time on every model and gives only launch prices; and the cited 3dcalculators.com guide, whose only timed figures are Plus4 listing and owner numbers ('about 8 min to 65 °C', 'about 5 min to about 60 °C', and 'within 10 min to a 60 °C sensor reading' in a test where the sensor read high) and which calls Bambu H2D/H2S times 'Not published'. ChatGPT's '~20 min' for the X2D appears in none of the 12 results. None of these pages gives a thermocouple measurement for any Bambu model, the effect of bed heating, or today's prices.
decides: This narrows ChatGPT's Plus4 pick rather than confirming it. With the bed running, the X2D reaches a real 65 °C in about 10 minutes (CNC Kitchen: 'roughly half' of 20 min). The Plus4's best owner figure is under 10 minutes to a 60 °C reading on a sensor that read high, with print-ready at 16 min 30 s. So the two are about level on chamber heat-up, and the X2D's figure was measured more strictly. The X2D also costs $60 less today ($589 at 3D Universe against $649 at QIDI US). The page should call the Plus4 and X2D a near-tie on chamber heat-up, say the X2D's time is the better-measured one, and note it is cheaper today. QIDI's own pages give heater wattage (Plus4: 400 W) but no heat-up time.

findings.label: Measured chamber heat-up to 65 °C
findings.value: about 20 min with the chamber heater alone; roughly half that (about 10 min) with the heated bed also running
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab X2D Review: Dual Nozzle, One Catch (CNC Kitchen, 2026-04-14)
findings.note: CNC Kitchen placed thermocouples in the chamber and wrote: 'it reached a real 65 degrees in around 20 minutes with the heater alone' and 'the heated bed running … cuts the heat-up time roughly in half.' The ~10 min figure is my arithmetic from 'roughly half', not a separately quoted number.

findings.label: Measured power draw
findings.value: 14 W idle; about 160 W printing PLA; about 330 W printing ASA with a 65 °C chamber and 110 °C bed; over 1,500 W peak during warm-up
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab X2D Review: Dual Nozzle, One Catch (CNC Kitchen)
findings.note: CNC Kitchen's own measurements. The 1,500 W peak is the draw while everything heats at once.
